name: Morse cluster global minima across the range of the potential
description: Find the lowest-energy arrangements of 38 to 80 atoms bound by Morse potentials of long, medium and short range (six instances). Energies are recomputed exactly and compared with the putative global minima of Doye and Wales.

requirements.datasets: None; reference energies are published values embedded in the evaluator.

sources.locator: Doye and Wales (1997): Morse potential in reduced units, Table 1 of putative global minima for N <= 80 at rho = 3, 6, 10, 14 (arXiv cond-mat/9709201).
LaTeX source of Table 1, from which the six reference energies (six decimals) were read.

limitations: The references are the 1997 putative minima; the Cambridge Cluster Database listed the same six energies on 2026-11-24, so no later improvement is recorded for these instances, and a score below zero would be a new putative minimum that needs independent confirmation. rho = 14, where later work reported new minima, is not used.

The putative minima are published with coordinates in the database, so a candidate that reproduces remembered structures scores well without searching; scores measure constructions, not search efficiency.
The score averages relative energy excesses (percent of |E|) over six instances with a 300 s budget for all of them; results depend on the machine speed for time-limited searches.

state_of_the_art.statement: Matching the six putative global minima of Doye and Wales (1997) gives 0; the Cambridge Cluster Database listed the same six energies on 2026-11-24 and no lower energies for these instances were found in the literature.

sources.title: Structural consequences of the range of the interatomic potential: a menagerie of clusters

name: Sutton-Chen transition-metal cluster global minima
description: Find the lowest-energy structures of 38- to 80-atom clusters of the Sutton-Chen many-body metal potential with the silver, nickel and gold parameter sets (six instances). Energies are recomputed exactly and compared with the putative global minima of Doye and Wales.

requirements.datasets: None; reference energies are published values embedded in the evaluator.

sources.locator: Doye and Wales (1998): Sutton-Chen 12-6, 9-6 and 10-8 clusters, table of putative global minima for N <= 80 (arXiv cond-mat/9711038).
Sutton and Chen (1990): the long-range Finnis-Sinclair potential and its (n, m, c) parameters.
Lopez-Castro, Ortiz-Chi and Merino (2024): GrowPAL search over Sutton-Chen clusters with 5-80 atoms; reports new lower minima for 12-6 N = 68 and 10-8 N = 58 (not used here).
LaTeX source of the global-minimum table (four decimals).

limitations: References are the 1998 putative minima (four decimals); the Cambridge Cluster Database listed the same six energies on 2026-11-24, and its coordinate files score them with this evaluator within 5e-5. Lopez-Castro et al. (2024) report database-level minima for all sizes from 5 to 80 except three (lower energies for 12-6 N = 68 and 10-8 N = 58, not reproduced for 10-8 N = 60); those three are excluded.
Putative minima are public, so remembered structures score well without search; the energy is computed without a cutoff, as in the source, and differs from implementations that truncate the sums.
The score averages relative energy excesses over six instances within a shared 300 s budget.

state_of_the_art.statement: Matching the six putative global minima of Doye and Wales (1998) gives 0. The 2024 GrowPAL search reports lower energies than the Cambridge Cluster Database only for sizes not used here; the database entries for the six sizes used here equal the 1998 table (read on 2026-11-24).

name: Dzugutov cluster global minima (polytetrahedral model metal)
description: Find the lowest-energy structures of 38- to 60-atom clusters bound by the Dzugutov potential, a model of glass- and quasicrystal-forming metals whose energy maximum favours polytetrahedral order (six instances). Energies are recomputed exactly and compared with the putative global minima of Doye, Wales and Simdyankin.

requirements.datasets: None; reference energies are published values embedded in the evaluator.

sources.locator: Doye, Wales and Simdyankin (2001): Dzugutov potential parameters and table of putative global minima for N = 3-100 (arXiv cond-mat/0011018).
Dzugutov (1992): the pair potential designed to suppress crystallisation in a monatomic liquid.
LaTeX source of the global-minimum table (six decimals).

limitations: The references are 2001 putative minima; the authors note that sizes above about 60 may have lower minima, so only sizes up to 60 are used, and the Cambridge Cluster Database listed the same six energies on 2026-11-24 (its coordinate files score them with this evaluator within 5e-7).
Putative minima are public, so remembered structures score well without search.
The score averages relative energy excesses over six instances within a shared 300 s budget.

state_of_the_art.statement: Matching the six putative global minima of Doye, Wales and Simdyankin (2001) gives 0.

name: Lowest-energy MMFF94 conformers of eight drug molecules
description: Find, for each of eight flexible drug molecules, the conformer with the lowest MMFF94 force-field energy while keeping the molecule's connectivity and stereochemistry. The evaluator recomputes the energy of the returned coordinates and compares it with minima from an extensive reference search.

sources.locator: Pracht, Bohle and Grimme (2020): automated search for low-energy conformers and rotamers (CREST).
Kolossvary and Guida (1996): low-mode search for efficient global conformational analysis.
Riniker and Landrum (2015): ETKDG conformer generation, used by the seed and the reference search.
Halgren (1996): the MMFF94 force field (RDKit implementation used here).
ChEMBL records CHEMBL941, CHEMBL192, CHEMBL1487, CHEMBL1229, CHEMBL83, CHEMBL1064, CHEMBL6966 and CHEMBL1404 for the structures.

limitations: The references are the lowest energies found by this collection's own reference search (ETKDGv3 sampling, MMFF94 minimisation and torsional basin hopping with three or more independent seeds; per-seed results in validation/chemistry-checks.json), not published values and not proven global minima; a negative score means the candidate found lower minima.

MMFF94 in vacuum with a constant dielectric favours intramolecular hydrogen bonds and folded conformers; the force-field minimum is not the bioactive or solution conformer, so the task measures search, not conformational realism.

Atom order and energies depend on the RDKit version (2026.03 here). Verapamil and ranolazine are racemic drugs of which one enantiomer is fixed. The time budget (300 s for all eight molecules) is checked only as a whole.

requirements.datasets: None; eight structures from ChEMBL are embedded in the evaluator.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published global minima exist for these molecules under this protocol; the scored references come from the collection's own reference search (validation/chemistry-checks.json).

name: Suzuki-Miyaura yield prediction on random splits
description: Predict the yields of 5760 Suzuki-Miyaura couplings screened by Perera et al. across electrophiles, nucleophiles, ligands, bases and solvents, on ten random 70/30 splits. The evaluator scores the mean coefficient of determination (R^2) over the splits.

sources.locator: Perera et al. (2018): automated nanomole-scale screening of 5760 Suzuki-Miyaura reactions; source of the yields.
Schwaller et al. (2021): Yield-BERT; the ten random splits (first 4032 reactions training) and published R^2.
Buchwald-Hartwig spreadsheet (Test1-Test4 sheets) and Suzuki-Miyaura random splits used by Yield-BERT (pinned commit, MIT).
Baraka and El Kerdawy (2022): comparison tables of published R^2 values on both datasets (Yield-BERT, DFT random forest, MFF and others), from which the comparison values were read.

limitations: Random splits of a full factorial screen interpolate between measured combinations of the same components; they do not test transfer to new substrates or conditions.
The test yields are public in the source repository; candidates or settings tuned on these splits overfit, so treat scores as development scores.

Published values were read from the comparison table of Baraka and El Kerdawy (2022) because the primary articles' sites were not reachable; they are compared, not reproduced, and no published predictions are available.

Candidates run in a separate process that never receives held-out values, but the process isolation is an audit-hook policy for honest program search, not a security boundary (ctypes stays available for scientific libraries); run adversarial evaluations in a container.

requirements.datasets: rxn_yields random_split_0..9.tsv (Perera et al. 2018). Fetched by python3 scripts/prepare_chemistry.py from pinned sources and verified by SHA-256 (catalog/chemistry-data-lock.json); not redistributed.

state_of_the_art.statement: No best-known value was verified. Published comparison values: Yield-BERT (Schwaller et al. 2021) mean R^2 0.81 +- 0.01 over the ten splits and the multimodal BERT of Baraka and El Kerdawy (2022) 0.833 +- 0.01; later work may report higher values, and this task's seed scores 0.823.
